paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah of Kefar Gavoria–Gibor Chayil.

A precious homily of his survives in [Megillah 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18a). He expounded: What does the verse “For You, silence is praise” mean? Silence is a remedy for everything. In [Ketubot 65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.65a), Rabbi Yehudah of Kefar Naviria—and some say, of Kefar Gibor Chayil—expounded: “From where do we learn that a woman is not allotted wine? As it is stated…” Perhaps the reading should be as in Megillah.[^1]

notes.text: The heading’s גבוריא־גבור חיל joins place-name forms; Gibor Chayil is not translated as the personal epithet “a mighty man.” The body’s נביריא is kept distinct as Naviria. Hyman stops after שנא׳ without quoting a verse; none is supplied. His final “perhaps” remains tentative, and he does not specify exactly what should be changed to match Megillah. The printed locators יח. and סה. are conventionally 18a and 65a; neither passage nor the place-name variants was checked against an independent witness.
